definitions.explanation: Describes an atmosphere or situation that feels tense or uncomfortable, especially between people. Often occurs after a disagreement, misunderstanding, or embarrassing incident.

examples.japanese: {喧嘩|けんか}した{後|あと}、{気|き}まずい{雰囲気|ふんいき}になった。
examples.english: After the argument, the atmosphere became awkward.

examples.japanese: {元|もと}カレと{会|あ}って{気|き}まずかった。
examples.english: I ran into my ex-boyfriend and it was awkward.

examples.japanese: {気|き}まずい{沈黙|ちんもく}が{続|つづ}いた。

notes:
WORD FORMATION:
・{気|き} (feeling/mood) + まずい (unpleasant/not good)

FORMS:
・{気|き}まずい (plain form)
・{気|き}まずく (adverbial form)
・{気|き}まずさ (noun form - awkwardness)

COMMON SITUATIONS:
・{喧嘩|けんか}の{後|あと} (after a fight)
・{失言|しつげん}した{後|あと} (after saying something wrong)
・{元|もと}カレ/{元|もと}カノとの{再会|さいかい} (meeting ex-partner)
・{秘密|ひみつ}がバレた{時|とき} (when a secret is revealed)
・{誤解|ごかい}が{生|う}まれた{時|とき} (when misunderstandings arise)

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
・{居心地|いごこち}が{悪|わる}い (uncomfortable feeling)
・{ぎくしゃく}する (to become strained/tense)
・{変|へん}な{空気|くうき} (strange atmosphere)

COLLOCATIONS:
・{気|き}まずい{雰囲気|ふんいき} (awkward atmosphere)
・{気|き}まずい{沈黙|ちんもく} (awkward silence)
・{気|き}まずい{関係|かんけい} (awkward relationship)
・{気|き}まずくなる (to become awkward)
・{気|き}まずい{思|おも}いをする (to feel awkward)
